title: Aggregates over ±inf: NaN
description: A `sum` or `mean` over both infinities is NaN, and `std`, `var` over a group with an infinity are NaN.

`Float32` takes the same generic code in single precision, so a `Float32` sum of inf and -inf is NaN too, on both engines, grouped and not. Nothing checks for the infinities; the Kahan step keeps its error term only while it is finite, so it adds no NaN of its own.

A `sum` of finite values that overflows is `±inf` without raising: `sum` of 1e308 and 1e308 (`Float64`) and of 3e38 and 3e38 (`Float32`, summed in `Float32`) is inf, grouped and not, on both engines. `mean` of the `Float64` pair is inf; `mean` of the `Float32` pair sums in `f64` and is the finite 3.0000000054977558e+38.
reference: `nan_creation`: raise (#257); a statistical aggregate of ±inf raises (`stat_degenerate`). ST-3 and ST-5 record that Substrait leaves both open.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: plain IEEE additions, no finiteness check
Kahan step: `new_err` kept only if finite
streaming: `+=` in the input's float type
pl.LazyFrame({'g': [1, 1], 'x': [inf, -inf]}) with x Float32 and Float64: x.sum() is NaN in select and in group_by, in memory and streaming

provenance.notes: Polars 2.1.0 (Python) from the project's environment, macOS arm64, `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=2`; each `LazyFrame` collected with `engine="in-memory"` and `engine="streaming"`.

evidence.note: pl.LazyFrame({'g': [1, 1], 'x': [big, big]}) with x Float64 (big 1e308) and Float32 (big 3e38); select x.sum(), x.mean(), and group_by('g').agg the same; pl.LazyFrame(...).collect(engine=e) for e in ('in-memory', 'streaming'), polars 2.1.0 → Float64: (inf, inf) ungrouped and grouped; Float32: (inf, 3.0000000054977558e+38) ungrouped and grouped; streaming the same
